rv.q: After the interval Maria Friedman’s production feels much more nimble and immediate. The highlight is a stunning rendition of Porter’s refreshingly naughty Let’s Misbehave — with twirling, swooping choreography by Nathan M Wright.
But not even Friedman’s ferocious eye for detail and the cast’s formidable energy can disguise the fact that the musical itself is a bit of a mish-mash tinged with snobbery.
Style and finesse don't figure on the agenda, from the minute the show shuffles haphazardly into gear.

cn.t: Critics find this Cole Porter musical energetically performed but fundamentally flawed, with stylish direction unable to overcome a patronizing, haphazard book—though the songs themselves still deliver.
